protocol.packageMetadataCheck: Package SHA remains in the disk snapshot; page release must equal package.version and the HTTP package.json path must remain 404.
protocol.flow: Load the same native main/mirror save, Continue, open Inventory, center-scroll the same lock button before timing, trust-click it, verify the exact committed state.

fixture.method: Seeded existing newGame/makeItem APIs; explicit floor 200, level 100 and gold 1000000. No removed fields or shortened equipment records.

protocol.exclusionRule: Only the one declared warmup per version is excluded. No slow-sample removal, adaptive sample count, rerun selection, or partial-success statistics.
protocol.lifecycle: One Chrome process, one isolated native context at a time, fresh context and reload for every scheduled sample. Warmups exercise this same lifecycle; they do not claim to warm the next document JavaScript realm.

clocks.start: performance.now() in the capture listener for the trusted target click, before the unmodified app click handler.
clocks.lastWrite: Return or throw from the final original native Storage.prototype.setItem call during this action.
clocks.twoRaf: performance.now() in the second requestAnimationFrame callback scheduled after the most recent write returns.
clocks.nativeSetItem: Sum of time immediately around original setItem calls, with exact original receiver/arguments and return/exception behavior.
clocks.longTasks: Native PerformanceObserver longtask entries overlapping trusted-click start through second RAF; raw duration and interval overlap are both recorded.

protocol.browserPath: Taskbook-authorized tester-provided Playwright/official Chrome. In round 07 the extension and cloud browser both returned ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED for the executor loopback origin; no user browser session is used.
limits: These are API submission and UI-frame latency measurements, not physical-disk durability, FPS, GPU or natural-player distribution measurements.
The operation includes engine transition, exact-snapshot checking, encoding, native storage and inventory rendering; it does not isolate TextEncoder cost.
The setItem wrapper records timing/counts and calls the original native method unchanged. getItem, engine, quota and Web Locks are not replaced.
Default Chromium quota is identical in configuration for both origins. Native failure to hold both real copies is BLOCKED, never bypassed.
navigator.storage.estimate is origin-wide information, not a measurement of the separate localStorage size ceiling.
One fixed seed and twelve pairs are finite scenario evidence. Keep all samples and do not infer a general speedup from small/noisy differences.
